attacksAttemptedAndFailed: That the subject moved. It did not — b447f24d… at start and end, 53007 bytes, mode 0444, and I never wrote to it.

That removing the expected.produced conditioning broke the cardinality table against the runtime rules. This was my strongest line and it failed. Read as requirements, 'exactly one qualifying primary' would contradict validationBeforePlacement.zeroQualifyingPrimaries, which permits zero and does not fail the output path. But the table is a set of case definitions over one declared domain — the siblings are the bare counts 'more than one' and 'zero' — and consequences live only in validationBeforePlacement. On that reading, which the domain member forces, there is no contradiction.

That the claude2v12 repair merely swapped strings and left the downstream qualified references orphaned. Refuted: honestyRepairsFromV12 is off-roster and unchanged, so I checked for the map Codex's second option requires, and idCollisionNote carries it — 'Claude v12 frozen file uses S-1 and ADV-1/ADV-2 (qualify CLAUDE-V12-*).'
That the ADV-SPC-V11-01 fold is again declared rather than performed. Refuted: cardinality.primary actually changed, and the repair entry says so in terms — 'Folded here, not merely declared.'

That the demotion of reMeasurementAtV13 lost the earlier live values. Refuted: the block retains its digests and head, and only note and standing changed, both rostered. Exactly one block claims LIVE.

That HEAD moving to 63518e5 or D-111 disturbed a pin. Refuted: file 08 is byte-identical across D-111, all pins re-verified against live bytes, and the artifact's own live block matches the current HEAD.
That the contract's substance moved under cover of a two-item repair. Refuted key by key: fifteen substantive top-level keys byte-identical to v13.

That a D9 code, exit, RunId, Finding or artifact-ref recipe is minted, that G17 is resurrected, that DR-122 is marked SATISFIED, or that a D-096 (A) grant is minted. All refuted by enumeration; QUALIFIED occurs zero times and both D-096 mentions are prohibitions.
The silent v13-to-v14 path. Refuted: seventeen changed paths, all rostered, zero escapees, with the machineSurface scope qualifier honoured down to the single member named.

That the accounting sweep clearing means the ledger is complete. This is the attack that landed, and it landed on the sweep rather than on the artifact: the sweep enumerates ids the records contain, so a record that omits an entire advisory roster passes it silently. That is how S-1 is invisible to the machine-checkability I praised at v13, and it is why pinChainRule says enumerate rather than merely qualify.

verdictStatement: Both Codex v13 findings are properly repaired, and both were findings my own v13 ACCEPT should have caught — I record that correction plainly rather than quietly. The claude2v12 pin now enumerates the frozen file's own roster of S-1, ADV-1 and ADV-2, with an explicit raw-to-qualified map added to idCollisionNote so the unchanged downstream references stay reconciled. cardinality.primary drops the expected.produced conditioning and defers to the runtime predicate, which finally closes the redundancy half of my original ADV-SPC-V11-01 — the half I verified at neither v12 nor v13 — and the repair entry says 'Folded here, not merely declared' rather than restating the old claim. The remeasurement chain is now explicitly single-LIVE with the prior block demoted, the roster holds at seventeen paths including a scope qualifier honoured to the single member, and the contract's substance is byte-identical across fifteen keys. My hardest attack, that removing the conditioning would set cardinality against the zero-primary rule, failed on the table's own domain member. What fails is one record. claude2v13 pins my v13 verdict at the right digest and records advisories: [], but that frozen file carries one advisory, ADV-1. pinChainRule states that every pin enumerates the full blocker, shouldFix and advisory roster of the file it pins, so the omission breaks a rule the artifact quotes — and it does so in the record added by the very edit repairing SARIFV13-S1, which is that same rule broken the other way. The string CLAUDE-V13 occurs nowhere in the document and no notFolded line names the advisory, so it is neither recorded nor booked, and honestyRepairsFromV13 asserts 'no additional v13 Claude findings', which is not true. An empty roster is the one form of this defect that every mechanical check I have passes silently.

coordinatorNote: REJECT of the artifact, not a disposition of the row. DR-122 stays OPEN at file 08 line 304; nothing here marks it SATISFIED, authorizes implementation, resurrects G17, mints a D9 or DR-006 recipe, or creates anything under D-096 (A). Two things the coordinator should weigh together. First, discount my v13 ACCEPT. Codex found two real defects there and I had the evidence for one of them printed in my own measurements and reasoned past it; the other was half of an advisory I raised myself and then only half-tested across two rounds. The lanes disagreed and Codex was right. Second, and pulling the other way, the substantive work in v14 is good: both repairs are performed rather than asserted, one of them explicitly withdraws an earlier premature fold claim, and the remeasurement chain now states which block is authoritative. The single finding is one record and three edits — record advisories ['ADV-1'] on claude2v13, add a notFolded line for it, and strike 'no additional v13 Claude findings'. On my measurement that takes the artifact to zero blockers and zero SHOULD-FIX. I would fold the duplicated guidance line into the same edit; that exact append-past-the-trailing-line mechanism cost the DR-101 lineage four rounds. One structural note worth more than any of these findings: the ledger's machine-checkability, which I called the durable gain at v13, does not detect an omitted roster — a sweep can only see ids that are written down. If the coordinator wants one standing rule from this lineage, it is that a pin's roster must be diffed against the frozen file it names, not merely parsed.
